prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere products, predictable latency, documented quality). External: spacecraft, launch segment, user processing environments. Elements: Mission Control Center (Bluebell): real-time authority, pass supervision, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, receives station constraint notices, hosts primary routing policy point; contacts: readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure; coordinates with PPF on mode/priority/gap changes; sends operational constraints to MPS after anomalies/outages/config changes; end-of-shift log of open actions. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; sends visibility predictions, orbit predictions, antenna pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse): processing, calibration, distribution staging; Primary (nominal)/Backup (failover, routinely tested) Processing Clusters. Network Control System (Lantern): WAN status, path selection, maintenance, station allocation, antenna readiness, contact start/end; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing refs, routing readiness; vets timing alarms. Long Term Archive: transfers rate limited during contacts. User Services Portal: receives observation requests, records request state. Mission Planning System (Cedar): authoritative timeline/contact assembly; receives booking requests, requests (USP or MCC), admission checks (authority, target, timing, mode, volume, restrictions); builds draft activity schedule. Command Validation Gateway. Telemetry Ingest Service: validates frames, produces Pass Replay Packet. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report. Product Quality Service. Ground Network Manager (Juniper): antenna assignment, arbitration, Antenna Deicing Notice, pins critical paths, consults Cybersecurity Desk. Antennas: North/South S-Band (command/telemetry; North nominal uplink) to MCC; Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band downlink, dual WAN to PPF. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team (console lead, telemetry engineer, systems engineer; reviews late requests; coordinates with Flight Dynamics Team before orbit control), Flight Dynamics Team, Payload Calibration Team (sends Calibration Patch Bundle), Cybersecurity Desk (Security Exception Ticket), station operators, subsystem specialists (reachable during critical/off-nominal), mission management. Escalation: console lead→discipline lead→mission management. Fault: preserve command state, no discretionary commanding, specialist review. Rules: daily cut-off; safety>timeliness>efficiency; X-band moved on precipitation.

New part:
S108: The draft schedule covers payload imaging, recorder management, housekeeping activities, and expected support from the North S-Band Antenna and South S-Band Antenna.
S109: For high-volume acquisitions, the schedule also accounts for downlink opportunities through the Kiruna X-Band Antenna and Svalbard X-Band Antenna.
S110: The Payload Processing Facility receives planning metadata needed to prepare downstream processing expectations without treating the planning schedule as a commitment to deliver products.
S111: The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are considered during planning only to verify that expected acquisition loads remain compatible with routine processing capacity.
S112: Juniper confirms that planned station use is compatible with network maintenance windows before the schedule is released for command preparation.
S113: The Spacecraft Operations Team uses the Antenna Deicing Notice to assess whether planned support can proceed without adding contingency contact margin.
S114: The Mission Planning System flags conflicts when two activities compete for the same spacecraft resource, ground station resource, or operational staffing interval.
S115: Constraint checking includes slew time, sun-angle limits, power balance, thermal recovery time, recorder capacity, command load size, and required separation between incompatible activities.
S116: The Flight Dynamics Team reviews cases where orbital uncertainty or contact geometry could reduce the execution margin for a planned acquisition or downlink.
S117: The Payload Calibration Team reviews planned calibration activities when they share resources with revenue observations or affect instrument configuration states.
S118: After schedule convergence, the Mission Planning System exports a command preparation package to the command engineering workflow at the Mission Control Center.
S119: The Command Validation Gateway, also called Osprey in this section, performs independent validation of command stacks before they are eligible for operational approval.
S120: Command stack validation checks syntax, timing, parameter ranges, sequencing rules, spacecraft mode compatibility, and consistency with the approved schedule baseline.
S121: The Command Validation Gateway rejects command stacks that contain unapproved manual edits, missing provenance, expired configuration references, or activities outside the planning authority window.
S122: The Telemetry Ingest Service is consulted for the latest spacecraft state needed to confirm that the command assumptions still match actual configuration and health.
S123: The Orbit Determination Engine provides the current orbital solution used to confirm time-tagged events, contact visibility, and any attitude-dependent observation geometry.
S124: The Product Quality Service may add planning feedback when previous acquisitions indicate that a requested geometry or instrument mode is unlikely to meet quality objectives.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
